summary: A contractor who builds or improves real property is the consumer of its materials and pays tax on them; its charge to the owner is not taxed.

conditions.when: Appliances (dishwasher, refrigerator, stove, washer, dryer and similar) stay tangible personal property even when installed, so their sale is taxed

citations.title: Utah Publication 42, Sales Tax Information for Sales, Installation and Repair of Tangible Personal Property Attached to Real Property (Rev. 07/26)
citations.quote: The contractor must pay sales tax on the purchase of the materials, while the transaction between the contractor and the real property owner is not taxable.

citations.title: Utah Publication 25, Sales and Use Tax General Information (Rev. 09/26)
citations.quote: The contractor is the final consumer and must pay sales and use tax on the purchase of materials converted to real property.

notes: 2017-07-01 chosen for consistency with the statute versions read; Publication 42 (Rev. 07/26) and 25 (Rev. 09/26) are current. Earlier date unverified.

summary: Labor to repair or maintain real property is not taxed and the contractor pays tax on materials; repairs of tangible personal property attached to the building (a furnace, a water heater) are taxed on the parts, and on labor unless it is separately stated.

conditions.when: Repair of the building or land itself (roof, wall, step, plumbing lines, repainting), where the materials become part of the real property
Repair of tangible personal property permanently attached to the building (e.g. a furnace or water heater): parts taxed, and labor too unless separately stated
Repair of an appliance (dishwasher, refrigerator, stove, washer, dryer), which stays tangible personal property: all repair charges taxed

citations.title: Utah Publication 42, Sales Tax Information for Sales, Installation and Repair of Tangible Personal Property Attached to Real Property (Rev. 07/26)

citations.title: Utah Publication 42, Sales Tax Information for Sales, Installation and Repair of Tangible Personal Property Attached to Real Property (Rev. 07/26)
citations.quote: Labor to service, repair or renovate tangible personal property attached to real property, if the labor charges are separately stated on the invoice. If not, the entire charge for labor and parts is taxable.

citations.title: Utah Publication 42, Sales Tax Information for Sales, Installation and Repair of Tangible Personal Property Attached to Real Property (Rev. 07/26)
citations.quote: Sales and use tax applies to charges for parts used in repair or renovation unless an exemption from the tax applies.

notes: Whether a fixture is real property or permanently attached personal property is decided item by item in Publication 42's chart.

summary: A separately stated delivery charge is not part of the taxable sales price in Utah, whether the goods delivered are taxable or not.
